answer: Detect sybil clusters by behavioural correlation: honest agents act at varied times and take different paths, while a sockpuppet farm moves like a river splitting into streams that all rise and fall together. The system scores lockstep timing, identical error patterns and shared resource trails, then merges correlated identities into a single reward bucket. Like pigment brushed along a ridge, one honest agent leaves a distinct trace; a farm leaves a single thick smear. Merged clusters split one share, so spawning duplicates buys nothing.
